latest_release.name: Kody v2026.11.26
latest_release.body:
Kody v2026.11.26

This one is about native ground. Package apps used to live in a browser tab — now, as this rolls out to orgs, you can install one as a real desktop app: its own window, its own spot in your Dock or Start Menu, a menu-bar item, global shortcuts, and start at login. In smaller news, promo codes finally learned the difference between monthly and annual billing, and signup stopped re-checking your username every time you touch the email field.

## New

- **Package apps can install as real desktop apps.** On a package page in the Kody desktop app, **Install** now sits next to Open app. Installing gives the app its own window on its own origin — with its size and position remembered — and a native launcher, so it shows up in your Dock, Start Menu, or taskbar like any other app, no separate binary required. ([#5597](https://github.com/kody-hq/kody/pull/5597), [#5598](https://github.com/kody-hq/kody/pull/5598))
- **Installed apps get a permissioned desktop API**, so they behave like native citizens: web notifications (clicking one opens the right page), launcher badges, floating and extra windows, a menu-bar item with its own popover, up to eight global shortcuts, and start at login. Each permission is asked once in a native dialog and remembered per app — grants survive reinstalls and signing in or out — and an app with a menu-bar item keeps running after you close its window. Apps can also declare their launcher icon and menu-bar entry right in their manifest, so both appear immediately after install with no desktop code needed. ([#5599](https://github.com/kody-hq/kody/pull/5599), [#5600](https://github.com/kody-hq/kody/pull/5600), [#5602](https://github.com/kody-hq/kody/pull/5602))
- **Install links work from anywhere.** A `kody://app/<owner>/` link now reaches the desktop app whether or not the app is installed — if it isn't, the link opens the package page in its own window instead of the dashboard, so nothing you had open gets disturbed. And in a plain browser, the package page offers **Install** too: open straight into the desktop app if you have it, or grab the download. ([#5601](https://github.com/kody-hq/kody/pull/5601))
- **Promo codes know monthly from annual.** Annual checkout used to reject every promo code outright; now a code can be scoped to monthly or annual billing, and using it on the wrong one tells you which to pick instead of failing mysteriously. Codes can also opt into a campaign claim scope, so claiming one promotion no longer blocks you from redeeming a later, different one — once per person per campaign instead of once per person, ever. ([#5595](https://github.com/kody-hq/kody/pull/5595), [#5596](https://github.com/kody-hq/kody/pull/5596))

## Improved

- Background cleanup of old audit records and package skill history now streams and deletes in bounded batches instead of loading everything up front, so large cleanups run faster and can't stall. ([#5603](https://github.com/kody-hq/kody/pull/5603))

## Fixed

- You no longer get a username availability check every time you edit your email during signup — the check now runs only when the username itself changes, and the username you typed is never rewritten out from under you. ([#5604](https://github.com/kody-hq/kody/pull/5604))

<!-- featured-screenshots -->

detail.readme:
Your agents' cloud: the memory, keys, code, and automations your AI agent keeps, portable across every MCP host. Built on Cloudflare Workers.

--- Kody is Your agents' cloud: the memory, keys, code, and automations your AI agent keeps, portable across every MCP host. Built on Cloudflare Workers and the Model Context Protocol (MCP), it ships a TanStack Start website, Worker-based request routing, package runtime plumbing, and OAuth-protected MCP endpoints. The project favors a compact MCP surface with powerful `search` and Code Mode `execute` flows over a large static tool catalog. Kody works for individuals and teams (orgs, teams, grants): each account holds isolated packages, jobs, credentials, memories, and related state. Tests and fixtures may seed deterministic local accounts, but no account is privileged at runtime. The repo follows several [epicflare](https://github.com/epicweb-dev/epicflare) starter conventions. The repo is organized as an Nx monorepo, with shared modules in `packages/shared` (`@kody-internal/shared`), the origin app worker under `packages/worker`, sibling workers under `packages/platform-worker`, `packages/runtime-worker`, and `packages/jobs-worker`, and mock Workers under `packages/mock-servers/*`. Production topology lives in [`docs/contributing/architecture/index.md`](./docs/contributing/architecture/index.md). ## Quick Start ```bash npm install npm run dev ``` The dev server runs at `localhost:3742` by default (the CLI picks the next free port and prints the resolved URL). Wrangler handles the local Cloudflare Workers runtime and D1 database automatically. To scaffold a **new** project from the epicflare template instead, run `npx create-epicflare`. See [`docs/contributing/getting-started.md`](./docs/contributing/getting-started.md) for the full setup paths and expectations. Contributors and agents should start with [`AGENTS.md`](./AGENTS.md) for repo-specific guidance. If you are trying to understand what this repository is for, start with [`docs/contributing/project-intent.md`](./docs/contributing/project-intent.md). ## Tech Stack | Layer | Technology | | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Runtime | [Cloudflare Workers](https://workers.cloudflare.com/) | | UI Framework | [TanStack Start](https://tanstack.com/start) | | Package Manager | [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/) | | Workspace | [Nx](https://nx.dev/) + npm workspaces | | Database | [Cloudflare D1](https://developers.cloudflare.com/d1/) | | Session/OAuth | [Cloudflare KV](https://developers.cloudflare.com/kv/) | | MCP State | [Durable Objects](https://developers.cloudflare.com/durable-objects/) on `kody-platform` | | E2E Testing | [Playwright](https://playwright.dev/) | | Bundler | [Vite](https://vite.dev/) | ## Scope - Source-available platform for individuals and teams, not a general-purpose agent harness - MCP-first architecture intended to work across compatible AI agent hosts - Compact MCP surface area preferred over a large static tool inventory - ChatGPT is a likely primary host target, while keeping the server usable from other MCP hosts where practical ## How It Works ``` kody.codes → kody-production (origin: TanStack Start, /mcp HTTP, OAuth, email, queues) ├─→ kody-platform (MCP / mailbox / meter / repo-session DOs) ├─→ kody-runtime (package apps, invoke API, StorageRunner) └─→ kody-jobs (cron + JobManager; calls back via JobsHost) kody.run → kody-runtime (package-app zone routes) ``` - `packages/worker/src/index.ts` is the origin entrypoint; platform, runtime, and jobs have sibling entrypoints (see [architecture](./docs/contributing/architecture/index.md#production-worker-fleet)) - OAuth requests are handled first, then MCP requests, then static assets - Webhook ingress (including GET subscription challenges) is handled in the Worker `fetch` path before TanStack Start - Remaining website requests go through TanStack Start (`packages/worker/start/http-entry.ts`) - Client assets are bundled into `packages/worker/public/` and served via the `ASSETS` binding ## Documentation | Document | Description | | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ | | [`docs/contributing/getting-started.md`](./docs/contributing/getting-started.md) | Setup, environment variables, deploy | | [`docs/contributing/environment-variables.md`](./docs/contributing/environment-variables.md) | Adding new env vars | | [`docs/contributing/cloudflare-offerings.md`](./docs/contributing/cloudflare-offerings.md) | Optional Cloudflare integrations | | [`docs/contributing/project-intent.md`](./docs/contributing/project-intent.md) | Scope, goals, and non-goals | | [`docs/contributing/index.md`](./docs/contributing/index.md) | Developing and extending Kody | | [`docs/use/index.md`](./docs/use/index.md) | Using Kody over MCP | | [`docs/contributing/setup/`](./docs/contributing/setup/index.md) | Local development and verification | ## Contributing Outside pull requests to this repository need a signed inbound [Contributor License Agreement](./docs/contributing/inbound-contributions.md). Public packages do not use that CLA. See [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](./CONTRIBUTING.md) and [`docs/contributing/index.md`](./docs/contributing/index.md). ## License Free for personal, family, nonprofit, and classroom use. For any other use, email support@kody.codes. Kody is source-available under the [Kody License](./LICENSE) (`LicenseRef-Kody-FSL-1.1-ALv2-Personal`), the same license as the self-hosted [kody-hq/kody-celld](https://github.com/kody-hq/kody-celld). It is a modified [Functional Source License 1.1](https://fsl.software/) that limits the free Permitted Purposes to personal, family, nonprofit, and classroom use, including self-hosted deployments and modified forks you run on infrastructure you control. It keeps the FSL competing-use restriction, and each version becomes available under the Apache License 2.0 on the second anniversary of its release. Code published before this change stays under the standard [FSL-1.1-ALv2](https://fsl.software/), the license it was released under, including its two-year Apache 2.0 conversion. Directories with their own LICENSE file, such as [`packages/cli`](./packages/cli/LICENSE) and [`packages/dev-runtime`](./packages/dev-runtime/LICENSE), use that license (MIT). Third-party files keep their original licenses. Public packages published through Kody do not use this repository's CLA and have no license gate; that is separate from this repository's license. ---
